title: When does grievous hurt legally turn into attempt to murder
p1:
A serious injury does not automatically mean it is an attempt to murder.

The surprising part? Two people can suffer similar injuries, yet the legal consequences can be completely different.
p2:
Many assume that causing grievous hurt is enough to prove an intention to kill. That is not always true.

The key difference is the intention behind the act. Attempt to murder usually depends on whether the circumstances show that the person intended to cause death or acted in a way that was likely to result in death.
p3:
Courts often look at factors like the weapon used, the body part targeted, the force of the attack, the manner in which it happened, and what happened before and after the incident.

For example, a severe injury from a dangerous weapon aimed at a vital body part may point toward an intention to kill, while a different situation may remain limited to grievous hurt.

The injury matters, but the intention behind the act can matter even more.
conclusion: What factor do you think should carry the most weight in such cases: the injury caused or the intention behind the attack?
